# Mercer Lane Press — book or digital product opportunity evidence log

**Status:** blank gate. This is a decision aid, not evidence that a niche is profitable.  
**Use with:** [production playbook](../PRODUCTION_PLAYBOOK.md). Default to improving a proven existing title/tool unless the new opportunity shows a materially different, verified buyer need.

## Candidate and scope
- Working title / existing title to improve:
- Format: new KDP title / revision / companion workbook / existing digital product feature / new tool:
- Specific US or other target buyer:
- Their job-to-be-done in one sentence:
- Current workaround and its frustration:
- Proposed change that solves the problem:
- Date researched / researcher / evidence window:
- Existing Mercer Lane products competing for the same production time:

## Evidence and decision standard (November 2026)
For a **new KDP niche**, use a provisional **70/100 minimum** to advance to production consideration, **not** an automatic approval. Passing 70 requires all mandatory evidence gates below, a clear distinct reader outcome and final human approval. There is no score-only bypass for unsupported sales claims, a poor KDP account-safety profile or duplication of an existing Mercer Lane title.

| Factor | Maximum points | Scoring rule |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Repeatable buyer problem / specific reader | 20 | Full credit only with dated independent customer problem evidence |
| Verified paid market and competitor evidence | 20 | Distinguish current offer/prices from inferred units sold; no full credit from search suggestions alone |
| Genuine review gaps and differentiation | 20 | Specific attributable review themes and a substantive solution not already sold by Mercer Lane |
| Realistic unit economics / royalty / effort | 20 | Market-specific calculations, downside, production limits and available publishing slots |
| Deliverable feasibility, quality, KDP/account compliance | 20 | Originality, technical expertise/source access, compliance, auditable QA and disclosure |

**Mandatory gates (each required regardless of score):**
- [ ] Current competing paid offers checked with dates and URLs, with meaningful range of alternatives.
- [ ] At least one independently grounded buyer-problem signal, with limits disclosed.
- [ ] Real competitor reviews or equivalent first-hand feedback reviewed; never invented.
- [ ] Price/royalty calculations use named region, trim, format, page count, printing cost assumptions and dated source.
- [ ] Existing Mercer Lane catalogue checked for overlap, and limited paperback title slots considered.
- [ ] Independent **red-team challenge** completed, including the strongest case against launching.
- [ ] Source accuracy, rights, originality, policy/disclosure and production constraints assessed.

**Score:** ___/100  | **Gate result:** pass / fail / unknown  | **Outcome:** proceed to final manual decision / small test / improve existing / reject.

## Evidence of an actual problem
Find first-hand complaints, specific questions, review gaps or repeated manual workarounds. Record dated, checkable sources. A plausible persona or AI-generated complaint is **not** customer evidence.

| Date | Source / URL or internal evidence ID | Exact problem in own words | What person currently does | Confidence / limitations |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| | | | | |
| | | | | |
| | | | | |

## Evidence somebody will pay
Separate **interest** (searches, comments, impressions) from **purchasing behaviour** (verified paid solutions or orders).

| Date | Comparable paid offer / actual source | Price + market | What buyers really receive | Genuine reviews or evidence of purchase | Important caveat |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| | | | | |
| | | | | |

Amazon BSR may indicate relative rank at one point in time but is **not a verified unit-sales count**. Search estimates, anecdotal income screenshots, influencer case studies and AI virality scores must not be reported as actual sales. Keep royalty assumptions and currency clear; use current KDP calculators/terms when doing economics.

## Adversarial challenge — strongest case against this opportunity
This section must be written *after* the positive research and reviewed separately. It should challenge the assumptions, not simply restate generic competition risks.

- Most plausible alternative explanation for the observed demand (e.g. seasonal, algorithmic, an established brand effect):
- Evidence against paying demand, and where sales are only estimates:
- Strongest existing substitute or competing title **including our own catalogue**:
- Why the target buyer may not choose this product even if they need the solution:
- Most damaging critical reviews, refund/support reasons or technical limitations:
- Royalty downside scenario and break-even production/support effort:
- One independent fact or observation that would **reverse** the recommendation:
- Sources checked, unresolved data gaps and reviewer/date:
- Does the provisional score survive the challenge? Why?

- Stop rule if the evidence is weak:
- Quality acceptance criteria and independent checks:

## Decision record
Check exactly one; show supporting evidence and uncertainty.

- [ ] **Improve existing product first** — stronger offer, sample, screenshots, listing or marketing.
- [ ] **Run small low-cost validation** — real demand uncertain; don't build the whole product.
- [ ] **Produce** — differentiated problem and paying demand reasonably supported, capacity/quality gates met.
- [ ] **Reject / park** — insufficient demand, copied proposition, poor economics or unacceptable risk.

**Portfolio rule:** publishing more titles or adding software features is not the default response to weak traffic. Diagnose distribution, page clarity, existing customer problem, actual product value and proven conversion first. For new KDP uploads, check current account limits, slots, compliance and manual quality gates before scheduling.
